test_cases.title: getCurrentUser() returns name and email on success
test_cases.given: an authenticated session with a valid stored token
test_cases.then: it issues a single GET /api/auth/me request and resolves to exactly {name, email}

test_cases.title: getCurrentUser() throws a normalizeError-wrapped error on failure
test_cases.given: the GET /api/auth/me request fails (network error or non-2xx)
test_cases.then: it throws an error normalized via the same normalizeError pattern used by other userApi.js functions, never a raw stack trace

test_cases.title: getCurrentUser() response never includes role, id, or avatar fields
test_cases.then: only name and email are read/rendered; role, id, and any other field are never accessed

test_cases.title: Logout button calls userApi.logout() then props.onLogout() in order
test_cases.given: the Settings page is rendered for an authenticated user
test_cases.then: userApi.logout() is called first, followed by props.onLogout(), with no additional network request

test_cases.title: Settings.jsx performs no navigation or redirect itself on logout
test_cases.given: the Logout button has been clicked
test_cases.then: Settings.jsx issues no router/navigation call itself; the Login transition happens only because onLogout flips isAuthenticated in App.jsx

test_cases.title: Settings.jsx does not accept or branch on an isAuthenticated prop
test_cases.when: Settings.jsx is rendered with no isAuthenticated prop supplied
test_cases.then: the component renders identically to being supplied one, proving no such prop is read or required

test_cases.title: Loading spinner renders next to fields while getCurrentUser() is pending
test_cases.given: Settings.jsx has just mounted and the current-user fetch is in flight
test_cases.when: the page renders before the fetch resolves
test_cases.then: a spinner (reusing the existing .spinner class) is visible next to the name/email fields, not a full-page skeleton

test_cases.title: Inline persistent error banner renders on fetch failure
test_cases.then: a readable inline banner replaces the fields (not a toast, not a raw stack trace) and remains visible without auto-dismissing

test_cases.title: Current-user fetch is issued exactly once on mount with no retry or polling
test_cases.when: the component lifecycle runs to completion without re-mounting
test_cases.then: getCurrentUser() is called exactly once (empty-dependency useEffect), with no automatic retry loop and no polling, completing within the inherited 10s userApi.js timeout

test_cases.title: Current-user identity is derived server-side, never from a client-supplied id
test_cases.given: an authenticated request to GET /api/auth/me with a valid Bearer token
test_cases.then: no user_id or identity parameter is included in the request; the returned identity matches the token's subject exclusively

test_cases.title: No PII is written to logs or error messages on fetch success or failure
test_cases.given: either a successful or a failed getCurrentUser() call
test_cases.when: the result or error is handled by Settings.jsx
test_cases.then: no name, email, or other PII appears in any console/application log output or in the displayed error message

test_cases.title: Name/email fields use the details-item labelling pattern
test_cases.given: the current-user fetch has resolved successfully
test_cases.when: the Settings page renders the name/email fields
test_cases.then: each field uses the details-item / details-item__label / details-item__value classes consistent with UserDetails.jsx, ensuring consistent labelling structure
